newsitem.title: NEPAL: Asian Development Bank to fund Nepal airport plan.
newsitem.headline: Asian Development Bank to fund Nepal airport plan.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a soft-term loan of $27 million to modernise and expand Nepal's only international airport, the bank said on Friday.
"The Tribhuvan International Airport (in Kathmandu) will be made more efficient and safer," the Manila-based bank said in a statement released in the capital of the Himalayan kingdom.
The bank said the loan, released from its Asian Development Fund (ADF), will have a service charge of one percent per year and has to be repaid in 40 years.

The loan, approved on Thursday in Manila, will be used for the expansion of the international terminal, construction of a new cargo handling facility and creation of additional aircraft parking facilities.
It will also be used to improve airport safety and security, the ADB said.

The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) has provided a loan of $11 million and the United States also pledged a grant of $9.6 million for the modernisation and expansion of the airport.
The improvement of the airport is expected to boost tourism in Nepal, one of the world's 10 poorest nations.
Tourism is the country's major source of foreign exchange earnings. It plans to receive half a million tourists in 1998.
Nepal receives 60 percent of its development funds from Western donors, including multi-lateral funding agencies.
